verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four runs are measured before the coolant was switched: run one switched 4 May but the shorter time is recorded 'by 29 March', and run three switched 5 October but is recorded 'by 30 September'. Half the cases have the effect dated ahead of the cause.

The central syllabus 'doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year' and every section was marked to that syllabus, so a doubled grade incentive applies to all four sections and explains a 6-11 point rise in coursework completion without the lab kit.

The claim is about revenue per order, but every case measures 'units per order' (6, 4, 7 and 5 percent above). Under a pricing change units per order can rise while revenue per order falls (e.g. if prices were cut), so the measured quantity is not the one the claim is about.

The district 'attendance reward scheme ... tripled its payment that term' and 'every cohort was on the district roll that scheme covered', so a tripled cash incentive for attending covers all four cohorts and accounts for the 4-7 percent absence drop independently of the timetable.
